tables.name: recordings

columns.name: meeting_id
columns.note: PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES meetings (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- PK + FK → meetings(id). Enforces 1:1 at the DB level. -- TEXT + CHECK rather than a PG enum — volatile 8-state machine; -- enums can never drop values once added

columns.name: status
columns.note: NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ( 'active', -- Recording in progress 'stopping', -- User/timeout triggered stop 'draining_ml', -- ML session drain initiated 'awaiting_gap_upload', -- Gap plan computed, waiting for client chunks 'composing_audio', -- GCS object composition 'post_processing', -- Summary, topics, tasks generation 'completed', -- Terminal success 'failed' -- Terminal failure ))

columns.name: ml_session_id
columns.note: -- AssemblyAI session ref for pre-warm and drain -- Audio config captured at session start

columns.name: sample_rate
columns.note: NOT NULL, -- Carried through to chunk storage and composition

columns.name: mime_type
columns.note: NOT NULL, -- e.g. "audio/webm;codecs=opus" -- Sequence tracking — powers gap detection + AudioStoredProgressEvent -- (emitted every 10s so the client can trim its OPFS buffer)

columns.name: last_audio_sequence
columns.note: NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Highest sequence received from browser

columns.name: last_stored_sequence
columns.note: NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Highest sequence written to GCS -- Gap between these two drives recovery

columns.name: gap_plan
columns.note: -- [{start_sequence, end_sequence}] -- Write-once-read-few → JSONB over a normalized table -- Serves GET /meetings/{id}/recording/missing-chunks

columns.name: duration_ms
columns.note: -- Computed at stop from the delta

tables.note: Target schema copied from tdd/schemas/postgres.mdx; current implementation delta not assessed. Full SQL, indexes and rationale are retained in the source snapshot. Recording contract names highest_contiguous_sequence/missing_ranges/audio_version; this older SQL uses last_stored_sequence/gap_plan and omits some contract fields. See import review.
tables.description: Tracks a live recording through capture, recovery, audio composition, and completion.

columns.name: meeting_id
columns.note: NOT NULL REFERENCES meetings (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

columns.name: person_id
columns.note: REFERENCES people (id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- NULL when unmatched or exhausted

columns.name: speaker_label
columns.note: NOT NULL, -- Raw diarizer label, e.g. "Speaker 1"

columns.name: match_status
columns.note: NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unmatched' CHECK (match_status IN ( 'unmatched', -- Diarizer produced label, no match yet 'matched', -- Voice embedding match above threshold 'exhausted', -- Max attempts reached, no match found 'manual' -- User assigned/corrected via REST ))

columns.name: match_attempts
columns.note: NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Bounded ~5 per TDD

columns.name: confidence
columns.note: -- 0–1 cosine similarity -- REAL not DECIMAL: ML scores are approximate floats

columns.name: updated_at
columns.note: NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Prevents duplicate labels from concurrent ML write-back race conditions UNIQUE (meeting_id, speaker_label), -- matched/manual labels must reference a person — catches application bugs at the DB level CHECK (match_status NOT IN ('matched', 'manual') OR person_id IS NOT NULL)

tables.name: OPFS audio chunks

columns.name: crc32
columns.note: CRC32C of raw audio bytes, stored in the per-chunk envelope.

tables.note: Local binary-file envelope, not a SQL table. Source: tdd/contracts/audio.mdx, OPFS Chunk Storage Format. Sequence numbers identify chunks; the per-chunk envelope is CRC32C + byte length + audio. SHA-256 applies to the manifest and gap upload, not an invented per-chunk stored field. Trim only after contiguous GCS acknowledgement. No session recovery after tab close in v1.
tables.description: Temporarily buffers captured audio in the browser until durable storage is acknowledged. Each chunk contains a checksum, byte length, and audio bytes.

tables.name: GCS audio segments and composition manifest
tables.note: Logical object/manifest record, not a SQL table. Source: tdd/contracts/audio.mdx. 100ms frames aggregated into 2s segments (tunable 1–5s), then composed in groups of at most 32. SHA-256 is optional for normal segments and required for final audio. GCS segment cleanup is specified at 24h after composition.
tables.description: Describes stored audio segments and the manifest used to compose a recording, including sequence ranges, object identity, and integrity checks.
